title: Only 7% Pass This Nursing Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Ward Briefing, Body & Observations, Safety & Communication, Priorities Under Pressure, Final Handover across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Ward Briefing, Body & Observations, Safety & Communication, Priorities Under Pressure, Final Handover. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited nursing entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Healthcare procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

insights.overview: Your nursing score at a glance

nurse-r1q1.question: Which gas has blood picked up as it returns from the lungs?

answers.a3: Carbon dioxide

visual.ariaLabel: 750 millilitres plus 250 millilitres equals what total

nurse-r1q2.question: A jug contains 750 mL. Another 250 mL is added. What is the total?

visual.ariaLabel: Pulse was 72 and is now 88 beats per minute

nurse-r1q3.question: A pulse changes from 72 to 88 beats per minute. What does the chart show?

answers.a3: It decreased

nurse-r1q4.question: Your hands are visibly dirty. What is the appropriate cleaning method?

answers.a2: Wipe them on a dry towel
answers.a3: Wait until the next break

nurse-r1q5.question: A person says, “I’m worried about what happens next.” What is the best first response?

answers.a1: Say there is nothing to worry about
answers.a2: Change the subject to distract them
answers.a3: Acknowledge the worry and ask what concerns them most
answers.a4: Use technical terms to sound reassuring

nurse-r1q6.context: Person A is comfortable and asks for water. Person B has suddenly become pale and is struggling to breathe.
nurse-r1q6.question: Who needs attention first?

answers.a1: Person B, because the sudden breathing problem may be an immediate danger
answers.a2: Person A, because they asked first
answers.a3: Both can wait until the next routine check

nurse-r2q3.question: Which body system carries rapid electrical signals?

answers.a3: Skeletal system

nurse-r2q4.question: Where are most digested nutrients absorbed into the body?

answers.a3: Small intestine

nurse-r2q5.context: Earlier: breathing comfortably and speaking normally. Now: breathing faster and pausing between short phrases.
nurse-r2q5.question: Which change in this observation note matters most?

answers.a1: The note contains two time points
answers.a3: The person is still speaking

nurse-r5q3.context: Earlier: walking steadily and feeling well. Now: dizzy on standing and noticeably pale.
nurse-r5q3.question: Which detail describes a new change?

answers.a3: The person stood up at some point

visual.ariaLabel: Handover says left arm, chart says right arm

answers.a3: The chart has a border

nurse-r5q5.question: Which system allows pupils to respond rapidly to light?

answers.a3: Urinary system

nurse-r4q3.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the face. Which protection addresses that stated risk?

answers.a3: Shoe covers only
answers.a4: No protection if the task is brief

nurse-r6q3.question: Someone asks a sensitive question in a busy public area. What should you do?

answers.a1: Offer to continue the conversation somewhere private
answers.a2: Answer briefly and quietly where you are
answers.a3: Ask nearby people to give you some space
answers.a4: Give only the non-sensitive part of the answer

nurse-r4q1.question: What should happen after protective gloves are removed?

answers.a3: Only clean hands if the gloves tore

nurse-r4q2.question: Where should a used sharp item be placed?

answers.a3: Directly into an approved puncture-resistant sharps container

nurse-r4q4.question: Shared observation equipment has just been used. What is the safest next step?

answers.a1: Put it straight back without checking
answers.a2: Cover it with paper and reuse it
answers.a3: Clean it appropriately before the next person
answers.a4: Only clean it at the end of the week

nurse-r4q5.question: A coughing person seems embarrassed. What is the best response?

answers.a1: Tell them off in front of everyone
answers.a3: Discuss their symptoms loudly across the room
answers.a4: Offer practical respiratory-hygiene support respectfully and protect their dignity

visual.ariaLabel: Fluid chart records 800 millilitres of intake; output is blank although urine was reported twice

nurse-r7q2.question: What is the main problem with this fluid record?

answers.a1: The intake is automatically too high
answers.a2: The reported output proves the total was normal
answers.a3: The entire chart should be ignored

nurse-r2q6.context: Person A is comfortable with a routine question. Person B has new chest discomfort, looks clammy and says they feel faint.
nurse-r2q6.question: Which person needs attention first?

answers.a1: Person A, because routine questions are quick
answers.a2: Both should wait for the next planned round
answers.a3: Person B, because several new signs suggest sudden deterioration

nurse-r4q6.context: A body-fluid spill is creating a slip and exposure hazard in a walkway. A storage shelf also needs routine restocking.
nurse-r4q6.question: Which task comes first?

answers.a1: Restock the shelf because it was planned
answers.a2: Secure the immediate hazard and arrange appropriate cleaning
answers.a3: Leave both jobs for the next shift
answers.a4: Walk around the spill without warning anyone

nurse-r7q1.context: Person A is comfortable with a mildly faster pulse after walking. Person B is suddenly confused, breathing rapidly and looks pale.
nurse-r7q1.question: Which person should be prioritised now?

answers.a1: Person B, because several new signs suggest sudden deterioration
answers.a2: Person A, because their pulse changed
answers.a3: Both can wait for routine observations

nurse-r7q5.context: Person A’s observations are unchanged and they are chatting normally. Person B was alert earlier but is now drowsy, clammy and difficult to engage.
nurse-r7q5.question: Which change needs prompt attention?

answers.a1: Person B’s new change from alert to drowsy and clammy
answers.a3: The fact that both people were observed
answers.a4: Neither, because exact numbers are not shown

nurse-r3q1.question: A fluid total rises from 600 mL to 900 mL. By what percentage did it increase?

items: PERSON A::Alert · mild stable discomfort · normal speech
PERSON B::Pale · difficult to wake · irregular breathing
visual.ariaLabel: Person A is alert with mild stable discomfort and normal speech. Person B is pale, difficult to wake and breathing irregularly.

answers.a1: Person A, because discomfort always comes first
answers.a2: Both can wait for a routine check
answers.a3: Person B, because consciousness and breathing have suddenly changed
answers.a4: Choose based on who arrived first

visual.ariaLabel: Earlier alert with normal colour and comfortable breathing. Now confused, pale and breathing faster.

answers.a1: The trend is reassuring because no exact diagnosis is given
answers.a2: There is clear deterioration requiring prompt qualified assessment
answers.a3: Only the colour change matters
answers.a4: Wait for another shift before reporting it

nurse-r3q4.question: A 1.5 L record is 40% complete. How many millilitres have been recorded?

answers.a3: 600 mL

items: AIRWAY BLOCKED → LESS AIR TO LUNGS → ? → LESS OXYGEN TO TISSUES
visual.ariaLabel: Airway blocked, less air to lungs, unknown, less oxygen to tissues

nurse-r10q1.question: An airway blockage prevents air reaching the lungs. What downstream effect follows most directly?

answers.a3: The kidneys immediately form more urine

visual.ariaLabel: 0.75 litres plus 425 millilitres equals what total in millilitres

nurse-r10q2.question: A person drinks 0.75 L, then 425 mL. What total should be recorded in mL?

nurse-r10q4.context: A task may splash body fluid towards the eyes. Shared equipment will then be used by another person.
nurse-r10q4.question: Which response best addresses both stated risks?

answers.a1: Wear ordinary clothing and skip equipment cleaning
answers.a2: Only wear gloves and leave the equipment for the next person
answers.a3: Avoid hand hygiene because eye protection was used
answers.a4: Use appropriate eye or face protection, then clean shared equipment appropriately
